text:
jen: heads-up — Deploybot blocked canary for release 2026.03.19 due to SBOM/license flag. Hold until triage.

deploy-bot: [AUTOMATION] release=2026.03.19 environment=canary check=sbom_license_scan status=failed
```
{
  "package": "third-party-lib-analytics",
  "version": "2.4.1",
  "issue": "transitive license: AGPL-3.0 detected via dependency chain (lib-core->lib-util->third-party-lib-analytics)",
  "paths": ["/app/.venv/lib-core/1.0.0", "/app/.venv/lib-util/3.2.0", "/app/.venv/third-party-lib-analytics/2.4.1"],
  "suggested_action": "pin or remove; request legal review if staying",
  "scan_id": "sbom-75321f"
}
```

chris-release: ack. Is this a new transitive dependency?

maria-eng: looks like lib-util pulled it in two weeks ago via schema changes. small usage surface but still risky.

tia-security: ok, quick triage — we need: (1) impact scope (which customers see this canary), (2) whether any shipped releases already included the package, (3) licensing risk level. I can take legal ping after we gather scope.

frank-product: which canary cluster? customer-facing canaries for orgs A/B testing only — we should pause rollout to wider clusters.

jen: can we quarantine the canary and open a rollback? prefer a targeted rollback of the canary nodes only. chris?

chris-release: yes. Plan: 1) quarantine canary (disable traffic routing), 2) create rollback PR to previous image digest, 3) run perf tests on rollback, 4) re-run SBOM with higher-depth discovery. I'll start steps 1+2.

deploy-bot: [ACTION] routing=disabled scope=canary release=2026.03.19 -> quarantine enacted by @chris-release at 1746501802

maria-eng: command I ran locally to find origin: `pipdeptree -p third-party-lib-analytics --warn silence` showed chain. If we pin lib-util to 3.1.x the transitive drop goes away. Might be lowest-risk short term.

tia-security: pinning is OK as mitigation if we verify no functional regression. Legal: @legal-team please review AGPL impact if we keep it. If removal impossible, we need an exception doc and maybe remove the feature behind a flag.

frank-product: feature behind flag sounds fine for canary rollback path. If we pin lib-util and run tests, can we resume canary in <4 hours?

chris-release: opening rollback PR now -> https://github.com/redwood/release-manager/pull/412 (rollback to image digest sha256:aa11bb22cc33)

jen: +1. Also add note to release notes that canary was quarantined for SBOM/license triage to avoid confusion.

sre-oncall: once PR merges we should run `kubectl rollout undo ds/canary`? I can coordinate the rollout undo and verify logging. Prefer manual verify before un-quarantine.

deploy-bot: [SCAN] re-run scheduled sbom scan job queued (scan_id sbom-75321f-retry)

maria-eng: i'll prepare a quick pin patch for lib-util and run unit tests. If green, we can attempt a pinned-candidate rather than full rollback.

tia-security: timeline: legal pinged, will aim to respond in 2-3 hours. If legal flags AGPL as blocker, we keep quarantine and escalate to exec.

frank-product: good. I'll message support and CS to warn about possible rollback in the next 3-4 hours for affected customers.

chris-release: update: PR opened and build triggered. CI -> https://ci.redwood.internal/builds/98765 (running tests, expected ~12m)

jen: thanks everyone. Decision for now: quarantine canary, open rollback PR, try pin patch as low-risk mitigation. Re-evaluate after CI + legal. I'll update the release board. :eyes::lock:
__notes: thread follows release/security gate workflow. messages are short and in slack style. includes bot automation lines and code block for scan output.
